title: Mizani
subtitle: Offline-first Android budgeting for everyday money
description: Mizani is a native Android app for tracking income, expenses, transfers, refunds, and balances across cash, mobile money, and bank wallets. It helps people understand day-to-day cash flow and multi-currency activity while keeping the ledger on the device.
problem: Keeping a useful view of personal finances is hard when money is spread across cash, mobile money, bank accounts, and different currencies. A tracking app also needs to work through unreliable connectivity without asking people to trust a cloud account with sensitive records.
role: I built Mizani as a native Android personal finance app, shaping its core flows from onboarding and transaction entry to wallet management, insights, local security, and data export.
approach: Developed in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose and a local Room database protected with SQLCipher. The app works without an account or continuous internet access; currency reference rates are fetched only when requested. I added country presets, support for cash, mobile money, and bank wallets, income, expenses, transfers, refunds and adjustments, plus cash-flow insights, CSV and Excel exports, passphrase-encrypted backups, and optional PIN or biometric access.
hardestDecision: The core challenge was adding useful currency and recovery features while keeping the ledger private and usable offline. I kept rates as optional, dated reference data and built encrypted backups for moving or restoring records, without introducing account or sync dependencies.
outcome: Released as Mizani 1.0.0 for Android, with offline transaction and wallet tracking, multi-currency entry, cash-flow insights, exports, and protected backups. The app includes regional setup for Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Nigeria, Ghana, and South Africa.
whatIdChange: I would extend the insights with opt-in budget targets and recurring transactions while preserving local-first storage and clear export and backup controls.
